name: TextVQA
description: TextVQA contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text to answer. The dataset is designed to facilitate progress on Visual Question Answering models that can read and reason about text in images.
creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
publisher: Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology
citeAs: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach. Towards VQA Models That Can Read. arXiv:1904.08920v2 [cs.CL] 13 May 2019
rai:dataCollection: Images were selected from Open Images v3 dataset from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). A three-stage pipeline was used: (1) annotators identified images containing text, (2) 1-2 questions per image were collected requiring reading text to answer, (3) 10 answers per question were collected from different annotators.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Customer feedback data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from Open Images v3 dataset. 100 random images from each category were sampled, OCR was run to compute average number of OCR boxes per category, and categories were weighted for sampling based on normalized OCR box counts.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images without text were filtered out using forced-choice yes/no flags from annotators. Questions were removed where a majority of workers marked flags for: no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, or unanswerable. Hand-crafted questions with known answers were used to identify and filter out bad annotators.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: OCR model (Rosetta) was run on images to extract word tokens. Images were filtered to 28,408 images containing text. Questions and answers were collected through crowdsourcing with quality control measures. The dataset was split into train (34,602), validation (5,000), and test (5,734) sets with no image overlap between sets.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Stage 1: Annotators identified images containing text using yes/no flags. Stage 2: Annotators provided 1-2 questions per image requiring reading text to answer, with instructions to ensure questions require text reading and have different answers. Stage 3: 10 answers per question were collected from different annotators, with options to flag poor quality data (no text, not a question, doesn't require reading text, unanswerable).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% of questions. Human accuracy is 85.01% on validation set.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Sighted humans (in contrast to visually impaired users)
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rosetta OCR system for text detection and recognition
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses an important problem for aiding visually impaired users. The VizWiz study found that up to 21% of questions from visually-impaired users involve reading and reasoning about text captured in images of their surroundings (e.g., 'what temperature is my oven set to?', 'what denomination is this bill?').
rai:dataBiases: The model often predicts 'new york' for city-related questions. For yes/no questions, 'yes' is the more common answer (4.71% of dataset), though the model does predict 'no' frequently. The dataset has limited biases with respect to images and questions as shown by low baseline accuracies (Question only: 8.09%, Image only: 6.29%).
rai:dataLimitations: 8.9% of questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens, which the current model cannot handle. The model has strong dependency on OCR quality - if OCR misses text or misreads it, predictions can be wrong. Some questions require spelling correction or n-grams of OCR tokens. The dataset contains 26,263 (49.2%) unique majority answers, making it difficult to have a fixed answer space. OCR system fails at detecting rotated, unstructured (e.g., scribbles), or partially occluded text.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is designed to benchmark VQA models' ability to read and reason about text in images. Models trained on this dataset should be able to: realize when questions are about text, detect image regions containing text, convert pixel representations to textual representations, jointly reason about detected text and visual content, and decide if detected text should be copied as answer or inform about an answer in the answer space.
